findings.text: Exposes a query that given an APIC ID plus which-units and at-level domains returns zero when the derived level ID is out of range or absent from the level map or when requested units sit above the level, returns one when both levels match, and otherwise counts set bits for the lower domain inside the level window.
Maps a Linux CPU number to the CPU number of its primary thread by translating through the CPU to APIC table, reducing the APIC ID to core-domain level, then reverse-looking up the owning CPU.
Reports whether a supplied physical ID equals the APIC ID recorded for the given CPU, widening the table entry before comparison.

Defines a small read-only-after-init record holding assigned, disabled and rejected CPU counts plus boot and real-BSP APIC IDs, initialized to one assigned CPU with both APIC IDs set to the BAD sentinel.

Domain population is measured by weighting set bits in per-domain APIC maps; a level window starts at the supplied level ID and extends exclusively by two raised to the domain shift, with the count taken over that interval.

Early boot limit hook starts from the current possible-CPU count, collapses to one when maxcpus is zero or the APIC is disabled, clamps to the possible_cpus command-line cap, and narrows the system CPU IDs when below the prior value.
Uniprocessor restriction holds when no SMP configuration was found; Xen paravirtual guests bypass the APIC check, otherwise the decision follows the APIC-disabled flag.

Possible-CPU initialization fakes a boot APIC when none was registered, derives an allowed count from assigned plus disabled clamped to system limits unless restricted to one, publishes total and possible counts, derives package node die core and thread maxima from domain weights and unit counts, seeds CPU zero as possible and present, assigns numbers to disabled CPUs from unmarked SMT bits, then marks each allowed CPU possible with primary-thread and presence state.
Scan context pairs a CPU info pointer with per-domain shift and CPU-count arrays, a legacy logical-processor shift from CPUID leaf one, and AMD package node count plus node identifier fields.
Relative domain identifier leaves SMT IDs unshifted, otherwise shifts right by the preceding domain shift and masks to the domain size minus one.
The header provides a degenerate unit-count query that unconditionally reports one, independent of APIC ID or domain arguments.

Firmware type codes are fixed as invalid zero, SMT one, core two, module and AMD CCD sharing three with the 0B maximum, tile and AMD socket sharing four, die sharing five with the 80000026 maximum, die-group six, and 1F maximum seven.

Two constant tables translate firmware type codes to internal topology domains, one for leaves 0B and 1F covering SMT core module tile die and die-group, and one for leaf 80000026 covering SMT core CCD-as-tile and socket-as-die.

Transmeta early probe reads the vendor maximum leaf, and when the family matches and at least the first extended leaf exists, captures its EDX capability word into the per-CPU capability slot for that leaf.

Transmeta CPU init refreshes early capabilities, sizes caches, logs processor and Code Morphing revisions and a 64-character identification string when the corresponding vendor leaves exist, briefly reveals hidden features through a vendor MSR around a leaf-one refresh before restoring it, forces constant TSC, and disables address-space randomization where sysctl support exists.
CPU device descriptor binds vendor name Transmeta, two identification strings, early and full init callbacks, and the Transmeta vendor identifier.

TSX control occupies auto, enable, disable, RTM-always-abort and not-supported states with a read-only-after-init current state defaulted by build configuration; the command-line parser moves it to enable on on, disable on off, auto on auto, and disable with an error on any other string, rejecting a null argument.

UMWAIT control defaults to C02 enable value zero and a cached control word for maximum time one hundred thousand; the encoding masks the time field and ORs the C02-disable bit, with helpers to test C02 enable and extract the time portion.

A dedicated mutex serializes sysfs stores that change the cached UMWAIT control; the cached word is accessed with once primitives, MSR propagation runs on every CPU, and the low-level MSR writer requires interrupts disabled.

CPU online re-applies the cached UMWAIT control with interrupts briefly disabled, CPU offline restores the boot-time original value under hotplug protection, and syscore resume re-applies the cached value after suspend.

Sysfs exposes a boolean C02 enable and an unsigned maximum time; stores parse with boolean and u32 helpers, reject times with low two bits set, and only propagate when the value actually changes, while shows format the current cached fields.

UMWAIT init exits when WAITPKG is absent, otherwise caches the original control MSR exactly once, installs online and offline hotplug callbacks, registers syscore resume handling, and creates a umwait_control attribute group under the CPU root device.
Steal-time area overlays a 64-bit clock with little-endian low and high halves, followed by seven reserved 64-bit words.
VMware ABI fixes information leaf 0x40000000, features leaf 0x40000010, GETVCPU bits 3 and 31, and stealclock results minus one for unavailable, zero for disabled and one for enabled.

Slow hypercall dispatches on the cached mode to VMCALL, VMMCALL or port-based I/O with magic command and four inputs, returns the primary output register, and optionally stores five secondary outputs through caller pointers.

Platform presence is decided by a version hypercall whose accumulator differs from all-ones while the magic register matches; the TSC frequency accessor returns the cached read-only-after-init kilohertz value.
Scheduler clock multiplies the raw TSC by a precomputed multiplier and shift then subtracts a boot offset; setup derives multiplier shift and offset from the cached TSC frequency at init.

Stealclock control passes a physical address split into high and low halves to the stealclock command; enable reports success on the enabled code, disable issues a fixed zero-one pair, and availability is false only when disable returns the not-available code.

Transmeta capability unhide temporarily widens the vendor MSR to reveal features, refreshes and samples leaf one, then restores the saved value, so interruption in that window would leave hidden state exposed.

Writing the UMWAIT control MSR outside the required interrupts-disabled context or without the store mutex risks torn cached values and inconsistent per-CPU controls because propagation relies on the cached word.
Global topology state holds a read-only-after-init system descriptor, an AMD nodes-per-package count, and a mostly-read primary-thread cpumask.
The possible_cpus parameter stores its numeric argument into an initdata cap defaulting to the build-time CPU maximum, later used to clamp early possible counts.
VMware scheduling-clock and steal-accounting default to true in initdata and are cleared by their respective command-line handlers.
